Today, picking a period ([globe-experience.tsx:390-399](frontend/components/globe-experience.tsx#L390-L399)) fades the whole globe out and pushes to `/story/[code]/period/[periodId]` after 700ms. questions.question: After the character fades in, how does the user get into the story?

options.label: "Enter" button (Recommended)
options.description: Character fades in with the era's name and a button under it. User clicks to go to the story. Fully user-paced, nothing happens on its own.

options.label: Auto-advance after ~3s
options.description: Character holds for a few seconds, then the story loads by itself. No click, more cinematic, but the user can't linger on the model.

options.label: Click anywhere
options.description: Character fades in; any click on the scene enters the story. Minimal UI, but less discoverable.

options.label: Stay — no story yet
options.description: The character reveal is the end state for now; entering the story is wired later. Also gives a back-to-periods control.

questions.question: How should the figure behave once visible?

options.label: Slow auto-turn (Recommended)
options.description: Model slowly rotates on its own, lit from the front. Reads as a display piece; no interaction needed.

options.label: Drag to rotate
options.description: User can grab and spin the model; idles with a slow turn when untouched.

options.label: Static pose
options.description: No motion at all beyond the fade-in. Cheapest, most poster-like.

content.text:
Done and pushed to `main`. Dev server is running at localhost:3000 if you want to look.

**What changed**

Picking a country still slides the globe left and shows the timeline. Now, selecting a period is a separate beat from entering the story:

1. Scroll/click a period in the drum → globe slides further left (`-58vw`, slightly shrunk) and the era's 3D figure fades in on the space it vacated, with the era name and note under it.
2. Choose that same period again (click the centered row, or Enter) → the existing fade-out into `/story/[code]/period/[periodId]`.

If you click the already-selected top row before any figure has appeared, that first activation summons the figure rather than navigating — so the reveal can't be skipped by accident.

The figure auto-turns slowly, and you can drag to spin it; a flick keeps gliding and settles back into the idle turn.

**Your model**

`raw/model.glb` → [frontend/public/spain/models/pre-roman-iberia.glb](frontend/public/spain/models/pre-roman-iberia.glb). I renamed it to the period id because that's the lookup convention — for the rest, just drop files as:

```
frontend/public/<country>/models/<period-id>.<glb|gltf|fbx|obj>
```

e.g. `frontend/public/spain/models/al-andalus.glb`. The extension is probed at runtime (verified: existing file 200s, missing one 404s and falls through), so **glTF, FBX and OBJ all work with no code change** — that covers the "not sure of the format" part. Period ids are in [lib/spain-periods.ts](frontend/lib/spain-periods.ts). Any model is auto-centered and scaled to a fixed height, so a 200-unit FBX and a 1.8-unit GLB read the same on screen; if one needs nudging there's a `figureTuning` map in [lib/period-figures.ts](frontend/lib/period-figures.ts#L33) for per-model `scale`/`rotationY`, and `figureOverrides` for filenames that can't follow the convention.

Eras with no model yet get a stylised gold placeholder figure, so the whole transition is testable now — scroll past Pre-Roman Iberia and you'll see it.

One thing worth flagging: I deleted [frontend/three.d.ts](frontend/three.d.ts). It contained `declare module "three"`, which — because `baseUrl` is `.` — was shadowing the installed `@types/three` and typing all of three.js as `any`. Removing it gives real types; `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint` and `next build` all pass.

Not done: the figure is hidden below the `md` breakpoint, since on mobile the timeline already takes the full width and there's nowhere to stage it.
Very good, can we try to put the person at the right of the timeline, and slide left the globe and the timeline instead of putting it at the left of the timeline?

content.text:
Rearranged and pushed. I drove it in a real browser to check — screenshots above.

**Layout now**: on reveal, the globe pushes to `-58vw` and the timeline slides left with it (`md:-translate-x-[30vw]`), leaving the right ~30% as the figure's stage. Before a period is picked, nothing moves — the globe and right-hand timeline look exactly as they did.

Your GLB loads and frames correctly, auto-turning (that's why he's in profile in the shot). Eras without a model still fall back to the placeholder — I dimmed its gold, since the key light was blowing it out to near-white.

Two small things I noticed while looking at it, neither fixed:

- The "Back to globe" button rides along with the timeline, so it now sits near the top-center rather than over on the right. Easy to re-anchor to the viewport if you'd rather it stayed put.
- Each era without a model costs four 404s in the console (the extension probe). Harmless, and it goes away as models land, but it is noisy in devtools right now.
but the person is too much to the side, and the timeline shifts too much
